PolyAIA — worked example

Yordi Tamayo

This is a runnable walkthrough of PolyAIA on a real mouse cortex dataset (3xTg / B6, control vs. alcohol; Sanna et al.). It starts from a pre-built Seurat object that already carries an annotated polyA assay, so you can reproduce the interesting part — differential polyA usage — without needing the raw 10X and polyA-peak files.

Because that object is already complete, the analysis comes first (sections 1–2). Section 3 then walks through the rest of the workflow: how the object was built from raw data, and the QC / integration / visualization helpers.

0. Setup

library(PolyAIA)
library(Seurat)
library(dplyr)

Load the example data

The example workspace (Seurat_PolyA.RData) contains everything the walkthrough needs:

Object What it is
seurat_polyA Seurat object with annotated RNA + polyA assays
rmsk UCSC RepeatMasker track (mm10), used in section 4

It is hosted on Mendeley Data and downloaded on first run (a few GB — the default 60 s timeout is raised, and the file is only fetched if it isn’t already on disk).

# Direct download URL for Seurat_PolyA.RData.
# Get it from the dataset page -> right-click the file -> "Copy link address".
data_url  <- ""                                  # <-- paste the URL here
data_file <- "rds_files/Seurat_PolyA.RData"

dir.create(dirname(data_file), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

if (!file.exists(data_file)) {
  if (!nzchar(data_url)) {
    stop("Set `data_url` above, or place Seurat_PolyA.RData at: ", data_file)
  }
  options(timeout = 7200)                        # default 60 s is far too short
  download.file(data_url, data_file, mode = "wb")   # mode="wb" is required
}
load(file = data_file)

The object carries the two assays PolyAIA needs, plus the cell-type annotations produced by Azimuth (CellType = broad class, Subpopulation = fine label) and the experimental design columns:

SeuratObject::Assays(seurat_polyA)

1. Differential polyA usage

This is the core of the package. DEPsMatrix() folds the whole APA analysis into one call:

  1. (optional) polyA residuals via PASTA::CalcPolyAResiduals() and per-comparison differential testing via DEPolyAPeaks();
  2. merging the results with peak- and gene-level metadata;
  3. pseudobulk aggregation;
  4. per-(cell type × comparison) RED / DPAU / gDPAU scoring.

Define the comparisons

One row per contrast. ident1/ident2 are the identity tokens built from condition_cols; treatment/control are the pseudobulk count-column prefixes (they follow the group.by order); Condition is the label. Any extra column (here Strain, Treatment) is stamped onto every output row.

comparisons <- data.frame(
  ident1    = c("Alcohol_B6",               "Control_3xTg",               "Alcohol_3xTg"),
  ident2    = c("Control_B6",               "Control_B6",                 "Control_B6"),
  treatment = c("B6_Alcohol",               "3xTg_Control",               "3xTg_Alcohol"),
  control   = c("B6_Control",               "B6_Control",                 "B6_Control"),
  Condition = c("B6_Alcohol_vs_B6_Control", "3xTg_Control_vs_B6_Control", "3xTg_Alcohol_vs_B6_Control"),
  Strain    = c("B6",                       "3xTg",                       "3xTg"),
  Treatment = c("Alcohol",                  "Control",                    "Alcohol"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
comparisons

Run

set.seed(100)

deps <- PolyAIA::DEPsMatrix(
  seu             = seurat_polyA,
  comparisons     = comparisons,
  genomic_positions = c("3' most exon", "Intron", "Intergenic"),
  celltype_col    = "CellType",
  condition_cols  = c("Treatment", "Strain"),   # -> "Control_B6", "Alcohol_3xTg", ...
  group.by        = c("Strain", "Treatment", "CellType", "Number"),
  gene.names      = "Gene_Symbol",

  # Residual background: Idents built as Treatment+Strain with no separator
  background      = "ControlB6",
  background_cols = c("Treatment", "Strain"),
  background_sep  = "",
  min.counts.background = 5,

  Pasta           = TRUE,        # FALSE = skip residuals/DE, RED from counts only
  modified_residuals = FALSE,
  min_cells       = 10,          # drop subpopulations with too few cells
  filter_method   = "edgeR",
  repeat_masker   = "Remove",    # drop intronic TE-overlapping polyA sites
  rmsk            = rmsk,
  return_seurat   = FALSE         # also hand back the residual-bearing object
)

red_scores <- deps$red_scores
polyAdb    <- deps$polyAdb   # analyzed peak table (for PolyAPlot)

Note: features is derived internally from the polyA assay’s Intron.exon.location (3’-most exon + intron by default, see genomic_positions), so no separate Peaksdb() call is needed.

The result

table(red_scores$Cells, red_scores$Treatment, red_scores$Strain)
, ,  = 3xTg

  End        87      80

  End       135       0
  Exc       683       0

  Oligo     321       0

Each row is one proximal/distal polyA-site pair in one cell type and comparison. The distal-usage metrics (all treatment − control):

  • RED — Relative Expression Difference, log2(d/p)_treatment − log2(d/p)_control.
  • DPAU — classic 2-site index for that pair, distal / (distal + proximal) (Wang et al. 2022).
  • gDPAU — gene-level generalization weighted by site position, 1/(n−1) · Σ (i−1)·pᵢ over all of the gene’s sites; equals DPAU when n = 2.

RED_Direction / RLD_direction label the shift as "Lengthened" or "Shortened".

red_scores %>%
  filter(!is.na(RED), RED_LRT_padj < 0.05) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(RED))) %>%
  select(Cells, Condition, Gene_symbol, RED, RED_Direction,
         DPAU, gDPAU, RED_LRT_padj) %>%
  head(15)

Summary plots

A four-panel overview of the RED results: how many polyA sites the analyzed genes carry, how the tested pairs split between intronic (REDi) and exonic (REDu) events, and the direction of the significant shifts in one cell type.

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)

### A. polyA sites per gene ---------------------------------------------------
# One row per gene (npas is gene-level, so distinct() avoids counting a gene
# once per pair/cell type/comparison). Genes with 10+ sites are pooled into "M".
p_npas <- red_scores %>%
  distinct(Gene_symbol, npas) %>%
  mutate(
    npas_bin = ifelse(npas >= 10, "M", as.character(npas)),
    npas_bin = factor(npas_bin, levels = c(as.character(1:9), "M"))
  ) %>%
  count(npas_bin) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = npas_bin, y = n)) +
  ylim(0,750) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkorange") +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.3) +
  labs(x = "poly(A) sites per gene", y = "Gene number")

### B. REDi vs REDu composition -----------------------------------------------
# Pie chart of the tested proximal/distal pairs in Exc: REDi = the proximal
# site is intronic, REDu = both sites are in the 3' most exon.
p_redtype <- red_scores %>%
  filter(Cells == "Exc" ) %>%
  count(RED_type) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = n, fill = RED_type)) +
  geom_col(width = 1) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(RED_type, "\n(", n, ")")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5)) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

### C. REDi distribution (Exc) --------------------------------------------
# Density of significant intronic events (|RED| > 0.25, padj < 0.1). The median
# annotation shows whether the shift is globally towards lengthening (> 0) or
# shortening (< 0).
df_redi <- red_scores %>%
  filter(Cells == "Exc" & abs(RED) > 0.25 & RED_LRT_padj < 0.1 & RED_type == "REDi")

p_redi_l23 <- df_redi %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = RED)) +
  xlim(-2,2) +
  ylim(0,1) +
  geom_density(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0.8, label = paste0("median = ", round(median(df_redi$RED), 2))) +
  labs(title = "REDi - Exc", x = "REDi", y = "Density")

### D. REDu distribution (Exc) --------------------------------------------
# Same for exonic (3' UTR) events, on identical axes so C and D are directly
# comparable.
df_redu <- red_scores %>%
  filter(Cells == "Exc" & abs(RED) > 0.25 & RED_LRT_padj < 0.1 & RED_type == "REDu")

p_redu_l23 <- df_redu %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = RED)) +
  xlim(-2,2) +
  ylim(0,1) +
  geom_density(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0.8, label = paste0("median = ", round(median(df_redu$RED), 2))) +
  labs(title = "REDu - Exc", x = "REDu", y = "Density")

### Assemble ------------------------------------------------------------------
( p_npas | p_redtype ) / ( p_redi_l23 | p_redu_l23) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")

Canonical vs. modified residuals

modified_residuals selects which implementation computes the polyA residuals that the differential test runs on:

  • FALSE (default) — PASTA::CalcPolyAResiduals(), the canonical version;
  • TRUE — this package’s CalcPolyAResidualsPolyA().

Both write the residuals to the polyA assay’s scale.data layer, so everything downstream is identical; only the PASTA statistics (p_estimate_PASTA, PASTA_padj, …) can differ. Re-running with the other implementation shows how much that choice actually moves the results.

set.seed(100)

deps_mod <- PolyAIA::DEPsMatrix(
  seu             = seurat_polyA,
  comparisons     = comparisons,
  genomic_positions = c("3' most exon", "Intron", "Intergenic"),
  celltype_col    = "CellType",
  condition_cols  = c("Treatment", "Strain"),
  group.by        = c("Strain", "Treatment", "CellType", "Number"),
  gene.names      = "Gene_Symbol",

  background      = "ControlB6",
  background_cols = c("Treatment", "Strain"),
  background_sep  = "",
  min.counts.background = 5,

  Pasta              = TRUE,
  modified_residuals = TRUE,     # <-- the only difference from the run above
  min_cells       = 10,
  filter_method   = "edgeR",
  repeat_masker   = "Remove",
  rmsk            = rmsk,
  return_seurat   = FALSE
)

red_scores_mod <- deps_mod$red_scores
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)

# A row is one proximal/distal pair in one cell type and comparison, so
# (Cells, Condition, p_peak, d_peak) identifies it uniquely. The pairing step
# uses counts, not residuals, so the same pairs are expected in both runs --
# an inner_join() therefore keeps everything they have in common and quietly
# drops any pair that only one run produced.
cmp_df <- dplyr::inner_join(
  red_scores     %>% select(Cells, Condition, p_peak, d_peak,
                            p_est_canon = p_estimate_PASTA,
                            d_est_canon = d_estimate_PASTA,
                            padj_canon  = PASTA_padj),
  red_scores_mod %>% select(Cells, Condition, p_peak, d_peak,
                            p_est_mod = p_estimate_PASTA,
                            d_est_mod = d_estimate_PASTA,
                            padj_mod  = PASTA_padj),
  by = c("Cells", "Condition", "p_peak", "d_peak")
)

message(sprintf("Pairs shared by both runs: %d (canonical: %d, modified: %d)",
                nrow(cmp_df), nrow(red_scores), nrow(red_scores_mod)))

# Correlation label: Pearson measures agreement in magnitude, Spearman in rank.
# Both are reported because they can disagree when a few pairs shift a lot.
corr_label <- function(x, y) {
  ok <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(y)
  if (sum(ok) < 3) return("n < 3")
  sprintf("r = %.3f\nrho = %.3f\nn = %d",
          cor(x[ok], y[ok], method = "pearson"),
          cor(x[ok], y[ok], method = "spearman"),
          sum(ok))
}

### A. PASTA estimate, proximal site ------------------------------------------
# Effect size for the proximal site of each pair.
p_est <- ggplot(cmp_df, aes(x = p_est_canon, y = p_est_mod)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8, colour = "steelblue") +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.2,
           label = corr_label(cmp_df$p_est_canon, cmp_df$p_est_mod)) +
  labs(title = "PASTA estimate (proximal site)",
       x = "Canonical (PASTA)", y = "Modified")

### B. PASTA estimate, distal site --------------------------------------------
# Same for the distal site. Worth plotting separately: the residual model is
# fitted per polyA site, so the two slots of a pair are not guaranteed to be
# perturbed to the same degree by a change of implementation.
d_est <- ggplot(cmp_df, aes(x = d_est_canon, y = d_est_mod)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8, colour = "darkorange") +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.2,
           label = corr_label(cmp_df$d_est_canon, cmp_df$d_est_mod)) +
  labs(title = "PASTA estimate (distal site)",
       x = "Canonical (PASTA)", y = "Modified")

### C. Adjusted p-value -------------------------------------------------------
# On -log10 scale, so the significant end of the range is the readable one.
# Zero p-values would become Inf, so they are floored at the smallest
# non-zero value present.
floor_p <- function(p) {
  nz <- p[is.finite(p) & p > 0]
  pmax(p, if (length(nz)) min(nz) else .Machine$double.xmin)
}

cmp_padj <- cmp_df %>%
  filter(is.finite(padj_canon), is.finite(padj_mod)) %>%
  mutate(lp_canon = -log10(floor_p(padj_canon)),
         lp_mod   = -log10(floor_p(padj_mod)))

p_padj <- ggplot(cmp_padj, aes(x = lp_canon, y = lp_mod)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dotted", colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dotted", colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8, colour = "seagreen") +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.2,
           label = corr_label(cmp_padj$lp_canon, cmp_padj$lp_mod)) +
  labs(title = "Adjusted p-value",
       x = expression(-log[10]~"padj, canonical"),
       y = expression(-log[10]~"padj, modified"))

p_est | d_est | p_padj

How often the two implementations agree on significance at padj < 0.05 — the off-diagonal cells are the pairs whose call changes:

table(canonical = cmp_padj$padj_canon < 0.05,
      modified  = cmp_padj$padj_mod   < 0.05)
         modified
canonical FALSE TRUE
    FALSE  4255    7
    TRUE      0 1135

2. Coverage visualization

PolyAPlot() draws coverage tracks with the gene’s polyA sites, peaks and transcript annotation. cell_filter selects which cells to show (a broad class or a list of subpopulations) and bulk = TRUE collapses them into one track; condition restricts the plotted region and site labels to one comparison, and adding condition_group_cols also restricts the coverage cells to the two groups being compared.

PolyAIA::PolyAPlot(
  seu       = seurat_polyA,
  gene      = "Mapk10",
  deg_list  = red_scores[red_scores$RED_type == "REDu",],
  polyAdb   = polyAdb,
  species   = "mouse",
  version   = "mm10",
  expand_bp = 2000,
  polyARegion = TRUE,

  cell_filter = "L2/3 IT",            # keep excitatory neurons
  cell_order = c("L2/3 IT"),
  bulk        = TRUE,             # ...as one combined track
  group.by    = "Strain",
  split.by    = "Treatment",

  condition            = "B6_Alcohol_vs_B6_Control",
  condition_group_cols = c("Strain", "Treatment")
)

PolyAIA::PolyAPlot(
  seu       = seurat_polyA,
  gene      = "Akap11",
  deg_list  = red_scores[red_scores$RED_type == "REDu",],
  polyAdb   = polyAdb,
  species   = "mouse",
  version   = "mm10",
  expand_bp = 2000,
  polyARegion = TRUE,

  cell_filter = "L2/3 IT",            # keep excitatory neurons
  cell_order = c("L2/3 IT"),
  bulk        = TRUE,             # ...as one combined track
  group.by    = "Strain",
  split.by    = "Treatment",

  condition            = "3xTg_Control_vs_B6_Control",
  condition_group_cols = c("Strain", "Treatment")
)

PolyAIA::PolyAPlot(
  seu       = seurat_polyA,
  gene      = "Msl1",
  deg_list  = red_scores[red_scores$RED_type == "REDu",],
  polyAdb   = polyAdb,
  species   = "mouse",
  version   = "mm10",
  expand_bp = 2000,
  polyARegion = TRUE,

  cell_filter = "L2/3 IT",            # keep excitatory neurons
  cell_order = c("L2/3 IT"),
  bulk        = TRUE,             # ...as one combined track
  group.by    = "Strain",
  split.by    = "Treatment",

  condition            = "3xTg_Alcohol_vs_B6_Control",
  condition_group_cols = c("Strain", "Treatment")
)

3. Workflow used to generate Seurat_polyA object

How the example object was built, and the QC / integration / visualization helpers. The steps that need the raw 10X .h5 files, polyA peak counts and fragment files are shown as non-evaluated reference (eval = FALSE); the plotting sections run on the object loaded above.

3.1 From 10X to an annotated Seurat object

seurat_obj <- PolyAIA::UploadSce(
  data_dir        = "../../Mice_example/2_h5_files/",
  file_pattern    = ".h5",
  metadata_file   = "../../Mice_example/4_MetaData/Metada_sanna.csv",
  species         = "mouse",
  reference       = "mousecortexref",   # Azimuth -> CellType / Subpopulation
  column_id       = "Sample_accession",
  genome_build    = "mm10",
  IDtype          = "ENSEMBL",
  remove_doublets = TRUE
)
# `thresholds` is the per-cell-type table defined in 3.2 below.
seurat_obj <- PolyAIA::SeuratPipeline(seurat_obj, sample_col = "Sample")

3.2 Quality control

QCPlot() shows the three standard metrics (nCount_RNA, nFeature_RNA, percent_mito). Passing cutoffs draws them as dashed reference lines, and split_by facets by any metadata column.

PolyAIA::QCPlot(seurat_obj, split_by = "CellType")

Per-cell-type filtering

RNA content differs a lot between populations — neurons carry far more transcripts than microglia or oligodendrocytes — so a single global cutoff over-filters the low-RNA types and under-filters the high-RNA ones. QCFilter() applies a different threshold per cell type: each cell is matched to its group’s row and dropped only if it fails a bound for its own type. Any threshold column you omit simply isn’t enforced.

thresholds <- data.frame(
  CellType     = c("Astro",  "End", "Exc",  "Inh",      "Mic",  "Oligo", "OPC"),
  min_counts   = c( 1000,     400,   2200,   1500,        250,      250,   250),
  max_counts   = c( 5000,    5000,   9000,   9000,       5000,     5000,  5000),
  min_features = c( 1000,     400,   2200,   1500,        250,      250,   250),
  max_features = c( 3000,    2000,   4000,   4000,       2000,     2000,  3000),
  mito_cutoff  = c(    3,       3,      3,      3,          3,        3,     3)
)

seurat_obj <- PolyAIA::QCFilter(seurat_obj, thresholds, group_col = "CellType")
PolyAIA::QCPlot(seurat_obj, split_by = "CellType")

3.3 Cell-type visualization

PolyAIA::UmapPlot(
  seurat_obj, "harmony",
  color           = "CellType",
  label_by        = "CellType",
  show_labels     = TRUE,
  legend.position = "right"
)

DotPlot() converts rownames to gene symbols internally (using the assay’s SYMBOL feature metadata), so it works whether the object was built with Ensembl IDs or symbols.

Gene_type_markers <- list(
  Astro = c("Gfap", "Aqp4", "Aldh1l1", "Gja1", "Slc1a3"),
  Exc   = c("Slc17a7", "Satb2"),
  Inh   = c("Gad1", "Gad2"),
  Mic   = c("C1qa", "C1qb", "C1qc", "Csf1r", "Cx3cr1"),
  Oligo = c("Plp1", "Mbp", "Mobp", "Mog", "Mag"),
  OPC   = c("Pdgfra", "Cspg4", "Sox10", "Olig1", "Olig2")
)

PolyAIA::DotPlot(
  seu       = seurat_obj,
  group_var = "CellType",
  features  = Gene_type_markers,
  dot_scale = 3,
  sizes     = c(7, 0.5, 9, 7)
)

3.5 Building and attaching the polyA assay

library(PASTA); library(Signac); library(EnsDb.Mmusculus.v79)
options(Seurat.object.assay.calcn = TRUE)

counts_dir <- "../../Mice_example/3_polyA_counts/"
samples <- unique(gsub("\\.tab\\.gz$", "", list.files(counts_dir, pattern = "\\.tab\\.gz$")))

# One sample at a time -- keeps peak memory low
polyA.assays <- PolyAIA::UploadPolyAAssays(
  samples       = samples,
  counts_dir    = counts_dir,
  peaks_file    = "../../Mice_example/4_MetaData/polyA_Bam_Files_polyA_peaks.gff",
  fragments_dir = "../../Mice_example/1_Mice_bed_files.nosync/",
  min.features  = 500,
  min.cells     = 50,
  genome        = "mm10"
)

# Unify peaks across samples, then requantify everyone against that set
PeaksFiltering <- PolyAIA::FilterPeaks(polyA.assays, multiple_samples = FALSE)

load("rds_files/Eviroment_seurat.RData")

for (i in seq_along(polyA.assays)) {
  cells <- intersect(colnames(seurat_obj), colnames(polyA.assays[[i]]))
  polyA.assays[[i]] <- subset(polyA.assays[[i]], cells = cells)
}


polyA.unified <- PolyAIA::RequantifyPolyA(
  polyA.assays  = polyA.assays,
  unified.peaks = PeaksFiltering,
  threshold     = 16,
  genome        = "mm10"
)

rm(polyA.assays)

polyA.merged <- merge(polyA.unified[[1]], polyA.unified[-1], merge.data = TRUE)

rm(polyA.unified)

annotations <- Signac::GetGRangesFromEnsDb(ensdb = EnsDb.Mmusculus.v79)
Signac::genome(annotations) <- "mm10"
Signac::Annotation(polyA.merged) <- annotations

cells <- intersect(colnames(seurat_obj), colnames(polyA.merged))
seurat_obj <- subset(seurat_obj, cells = cells)
seurat_obj[["polyA"]] <- subset(polyA.merged, cells = cells)
DefaultAssay(seurat_obj) <- "polyA"

rm(polyA.merged)

# Annotate sites against the polyA reference database
seurat_obj <- PASTA::GetPolyADbAnnotation(
  seurat_obj,
  polyAdb.file = "../../Mice_example/4_MetaData/polyAdb_mm10.txt",
  max.dist     = 50
)

# The example workspace bundles the object together with the RepeatMasker
# table, so section 4 can run straight after load().
rmsk <- read.delim("../../Mice_example/4_MetaData/mm10.rmsk.txt")
